_comment: One corpus, two readers. ConversationRecorder (PHP) and ai-bridge-chat.js
(browser) are independent implementations of the same protocol rules, and
every parity bug found in this area came from asserting by hand that they
agree. They do not, reliably, and a reviewer noticing is not a test.
Each scenario is a stream of events and the blocks both sides must end up
with. EVERY block and EVERY field is compared — an earlier version compared
four fields of one block type, which made it blind to the feature it was
The terminal is part of the scenario. Without one, `done` is appended.
Add a scenario when a divergence is found; both suites pick it up with no

_comment: The block has its own result and no verdict; the frame has a different
result and a failure verdict. Carrying is_error on its own labelled the
block's OWN result as failed, and attached the same flag to the orphaned
result below it: one flag, two places, wrong in both. is_error describes
a result, so it travels with one or not at all.
